scores.rationale: Several snippets bear on the link between transport-system complexity and maintenance cost. Snippet 18 explicitly states the DEB assumption that volume-specific maintenance costs depend on cell complexity, directly supporting the idea that simpler systems have lower maintenance. Snippets 1, 5, 9, and 11 develop the argument that passive diffusion is cheaper/'free' while active transport is costly and only favored as cells become larger and more complex, consistent with simpler/passive systems entailing lower maintenance. Snippet 8 (Krogh) notes that simple passive diffusion suffices for small organisms' maintenance, whereas active processes become necessary in larger cells, again aligning with the fact. Snippet 17 links maintenance overhead to extra transformations and compound complexity. None of the snippets contradict the stylized fact; the remainder are topically related (metabolic scaling, RTN/WBE critiques) but do not directly test the maintenance-vs-complexity claim. Overall the corpus offers moderate, coherent support with no conflict, hence corroborated direction but only moderate strength because most evidence is theoretical/assumption-based rather than experimental.
